title: R3: Shared pipeline integration and acceptance
global_constraints: GC01: Script CEO owns dispatch, scheduling, gates, authoritative state, commits, and publication; no coordinating LLM is introduced.
GC02: The Codex path never executes OpenCode or silently changes runtime, model, reasoning effort, or role.
GC03: Every role receives explicit model and reasoning settings; operator, reviewer, and director have separate identities and permissions.
GC04: Plans, specs, prompts, ledger summaries, and implementation comments are English; product UI copy retains its established locale.
GC05: Codex workers inherit no brainstorming transcript; all required task context comes from versioned artifacts and explicit packages.
GC06: Operator-owned RED/GREEN and independent semantic review remain mandatory; mechanical green alone never approves a task or branch.
GC07: Raw evidence determines gates; RTK only changes the model-visible rendering and never the command exit code.
GC08: Unknown, malformed, stale, interrupted, or mismatched results never advance authoritative state.
GC09: Resume is confined to a recorded task family and role; unrelated tasks and closing use fresh contexts.
GC10: Parallel workers use distinct worktrees; shared plan writes, integration, and publication are serialized by scripts.
GC11: Existing user changes, unrelated branches, Codex sessions, credentials, and installed plugin caches are preserved.
GC12: Jev remains optional advisory inference; it cannot dispatch, select a tier, approve, route, or write the authoritative ledger.
GC13: Each new run confirms local-only or push-and-PR publication and concurrency at launch; resume retains those choices and no automatic merge is allowed.
GC14: Compatibility is claimed only for runtime/platform/toolchain combinations backed by the acceptance matrix.

tasks.title: Isolate runs, worktrees and shared state with durable ownership
tasks.summary: Introduce canonical run/plan identities, scoped worktree ownership, strict plan validation and evidence-preserving integration. Repair cross-plan collisions and mixed-toolchain gate propagation while retaining the current deterministic scheduler.
acceptance: Validate initial and refreshed plans with one strict validator for fields, IDs, DAG, spec paths/anchors, canonical touches and verification metadata. Preserve explicit non-authoritative extensions and reject unsupported runtime controls.

Namespace plan workspace by canonical plan path/repository identity and worktree/branch by run/family. Codex branch names use codex/pipeline; every consumer resolves persisted ownership rather than task/N string reconstruction.

Lock the integration writer by repository/branch with owner PID/start/run identity. Concurrent runs on the same integration branch block; unrelated runs/branches and same-basename plans cannot reuse each other's state.

Scheduler conflicts include declared implementation paths, new-test paths and shared write resources. Explicit existing-test updates require reviewed declaration. Operator plan writes are rejected despite the legacy plan-path exemption.

Copy all resolved toolchains to workers and run all affected integration toolchains; preserve raw evidence and exact-tree reuse conditions. Rebuild nonportable Flutter caches when paths do not validate.
Keep dirty-tree integration rejection and bounded recovery. Orphan branches, mismatched worktree ownership, missing paths or corrupt ledger state fail closed before any destructive action.

Export and validate all task-family logs/results/session manifests/shards before release. Require stopped workers, clean worktree, complete family approval, and merged tip. Remove no unrelated/dirty worktree and never use unconditional force removal.

Ledger writes remain script-owned, locked and recoverable; partial partition writes can be rebuilt from the authoritative log without fabricating approvals. Do not ignore required state-write failures.

Tests cover same basename in two directories, task ID 1 in two distinct plans, concurrent owner claims, Windows case/path aliases, disjoint tests, orphan branch reuse, evidence export failure and mixed-language integration.
Apply shared engine behavior to both explicitly selected backends. Use R1 backend-neutral configuration and R2 adapters; retain conservative full-suite gates until R4.

Allow related new files through supervisor-issued path grants within task-approved roots; do not add a director dispatch solely for a new related path. Undeclared existing-file changes require a director scope proposal. Acquire canonical path ownership atomically, check protected paths and active/future task conflicts, and persist grants across resume.

tasks.title: Wire normalized outcomes into RED, GREEN and independent review
tasks.summary: Adapt every generic and Flutter gate path to the new outcomes, with durable candidate identity and explicit review-pending recovery. Stop parsing OpenCode events on the Codex path and stop swallowing reviewer launch failures.
acceptance: Codex operator status comes from the validated final object. TEST_DEFECT routes arbitration, BLOCKED preserves an actionable block, and DONE still requires authoritative RED-form and GREEN checks.

Execute configured argv-based gates with raw exits; preserve compression-only RTK semantics and scope checks. Green, commit success, reviewer transport success, reviewer APPROVED and task_complete are separate barriers.

Remove swallowed reviewer failures from both generic and Flutter Codex branches. A failed reviewer dispatch remains review-pending and resumes/retries the review without a new coder attempt or a new commit.

Persist original attempt base, candidate HEAD and plan/context hashes. Recovery after a post-commit failure reviews the complete intended diff rather than recomputing base from the already-committed HEAD.

Codex parse-review consumes strict normalized results and current attempt binding; legacy OpenCode logs remain on their explicit parser path. Reject malformed APPROVED and a valid verdict belonging to an old candidate.
Review packages carry complete brief/spec/global constraints, full diff including tests, gate/evidence metadata and optional Jev guidance. Jev failures preserve standard mandatory review.

Review sessions remain role-separated and may resume only inside the same family with a fully refreshed package. Existing arbitration evidence archives and bounded re-escalation behavior are preserved.
No-op verification tasks require explicit plan semantics and independent review; ordinary tasks cannot invent RED evidence or bypass failed/empty commit barriers.

Tests cover both language branches, reviewer failure after commit, replayed old verdict, BLOCKED/TEST_DEFECT routing, unchanged candidate recovery, and negative semantic results with transport exit 0.

tasks.title: Apply director proposals through canonical script transactions
tasks.summary: Change Codex correction/arbitration from model edits into validated proposals applied by one canonical plan writer. Preserve task-family continuation and reconcile plan commits, ledger events and snapshots after interruption.
acceptance: On the Codex path director invocations are read-only, receive full current plan and scoped evidence, and return the task-2 proposal schema. Never ask a director to mutate tracked plan or authoritative ledger directly.

apply_director_proposal holds the canonical integration lock, validates source hash/target/allowed changes/spec scope/DAG, allocates the next ID and atomically commits plan changes. Stale proposals are re-requested, not silently rebased.

Two simultaneous worktree corrective proposals cannot allocate duplicate IDs or overwrite each other. Workers update derived snapshots at episode boundaries and keep their tracked plan files unchanged.

Corrective children remain in the original family worktree and continue only its operator session. Persist family membership and valid predecessor requirements; never make a corrective depend on its own incomplete parent.

Journal proposal identity, old/new plan hashes, assigned IDs, plan commit and state events. Restart after each transaction boundary yields exactly one applied proposal and no false arbitrate_resolved.

Valid director rulings resume the recorded task episode without resetting its cumulative coder budget. Support cycle limits [5,3,3]; after the third exhausted cycle and director assessment pause. Invalid proposals or unresolved blockers cannot restart a loop.
Jev Site 3 is consulted only at a required director boundary, with bound episode/context. Off/shadow/failure preserves that call; in-scope direct corrections do not run director guidance.

Tests cover concurrent corrective proposals, stale plan hashes, unsupported field changes, dependency cycles, crash after commit before ledger, family resume identity and corrective-parent reconciliation.

Resolve undeclared existing-file scope changes through locked proposals without incrementing task identity to evade budgets. Compatible, license-approved dependency additions do not require user approval, but shared manifest/lockfile edits require coordinated scope grants.

tasks.title: Connect the complete Codex launcher, cancellation and explicit publication
tasks.summary: Wire the shared pipeline state machine to the Codex configuration, direct worker backend, canonical plan writer, isolated waves and strict closing. Add durable run control and a Windows launcher without requiring an interactive model in the runtime loop.
acceptance: Expose run-codex-pipeline PLAN --config FILE [--max-parallel N] [--publication local|pull_request] and equivalent PowerShell entry. Select Codex before any setup/dispatch and fail if unavailable; never launch opencode.

Preflight complete plan/config/policy/toolchains and persist the pinned run manifest. At each new run ask backend/model roles, publication local or pull_request, and concurrency; offer saved model choices. No implicit two-worker or local-only selection; headless launches require explicitly confirmed configuration.

Track every task-run and Codex process by owned identity; cancellation stops new admissions and owned trees, waits for termination and records interrupted state. Windows launch stays hidden; never terminate a process by name alone.

Resume from durable state with no caller chat dependency, reject a second active integration owner, refresh canonical plan after transactions/integration, and never interpret a missing task-run exit record as success.

Run serial and parallel flows with full toolchain and config propagation. Integration and canonical plan transactions share one exclusion boundary; successful sibling work remains recoverable after a failure.

Honor configured deadlines, quota/provider/policy failures and bounded transport retries. Treat the confirmed 5/3/3 semantic budget as the target contract; R4 enables direct corrections and full budget enforcement before production adoption.

Publish only after R3 task 4 candidate-bound approval and required verification/waivers. Honor launch-time local-only or push-and-PR authorization without asking again; no force push or automatic merge. Detect existing PRs idempotently and preserve resumable delivery failures.

Detect detached HEAD and other desktop-managed worktrees at startup. Require a named integration branch or explicit local-only handling; do not call desktop-only tools from the shell or promise native subagent UI linkage.
